items.title: Redesigned OLED MacBook Air Could Launch in 2027 or 2028
items.summary: A MacBook Air with a new look could launch in late 2027 or 2028, Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman said in the latest episode of his Power On podcast. Apple plans to refresh the ‌MacBook Air‌ with M6 chips in early 2027 alongside the MacBook Neo 2, but that update won't include a new design. A more extensive…
items.body: A MacBook Air with a new look could launch in late 2027 or 2028, Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman said in the latest episode of his Power On podcast. Apple plans to refresh the ‌MacBook Air‌ with M6 chips in early 2027 alongside the MacBook Neo 2, but that update won't include a new design. A more extensive overhaul could follow later in 2027 or in 2028, and the ‌MacBook Air‌ could get an OLED display at that time. MacBook Air is Apple's most popular computer, and they need to keep it very fresh. And so my anticipation is 2027, 2028 is when we're going to get the big MacBook Air overhaul. And I think OLED will be part of that conversation. Apple last overhauled the ‌MacBook Air‌'s design in 2022, eliminating the prior wedge shape for a more uniform MacBook Pro-style chassis. The machine adopted a brighter Liquid Retina display with a notch for the camera, and a MagSafe charging port. In 2023, Apple added a 15-inch model, but since then, we've only gotten minor updates. Apple just added ‌OLED‌ to the MacBook Pro with the launch of the 2026 PROLED models, so it's not clear whether the high-end display will trickle down to the ‌MacBook Air‌ that quickly. In prior reports , Gurman has leaned more toward the 2028 timeline than late 2027. Pricing on the PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌ starts at $2,899, while the ‌MacBook Air‌ is one of Apple's more affordable notebooks and starts at $1,299. Apple would likely need to offer a high-end ‌OLED‌ ‌MacBook Air‌ alongside ‌MacBook Air‌ models with an LCD display to keep the price gap intact. items.title: Google Home is sorting out issues with speakers, cameras, lights, and more
items.summary: Your smart home sounds like it's about to get a little bit smarter.
items.body:
Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Smart home

Google Home is sorting out issues with speakers, cameras, lights, and more

Your smart home sounds like it's about to get a little bit smarter.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 5:52 PM ET

•

•

Stephen Schenck / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Google Home is getting some new features and fixes for speakers, cameras, lights, and thermostats.

• Home Premium users will no longer have to configure all their cameras separately.

• Google’s smoothing out issues with transferring music playback to a new speaker or display.

Big changes are on the way for your Google-powered smart home, with Assistant finally scheduled to go away for good next summer — that’s still months off, though, and in the meantime we’ve got a fresh batch of Google Home updates to check out.

Today Google’s sharing its latest set of new features and bugfixes coming to Home, and it looks like there are quite a few in here that are worth paying attention to. For starters, owners of those affordable Walmart Onn smart cameras can now use Familiar Faces with outdoor models. Other camera upgrades include support for clip feedback when multiple users are configured as admins, as well as manual controls for camera security sirens. We’re also getting bugfixes for event notification previews, event-based video history, and camera controls in landscape view.

Home Premium subscribers can look for a new onboarding flow when adding multiple cameras to their homes, letting you configure premium features all at once.

Setting up a Nest Thermostat? Google’s adding a new feature that lets you clone daily temperature settings, so you can quickly apply the same options across multiple days.

We’ve got a few fixes and improvements related to speakers incoming. Google Home Speaker setup should now proceed with fewer visual glitches, and Google’s resolved an issue with configuring these as stereo pairs. There’s also a handful of fixes for audio issues with Google TV, and you should notice more consistent behavior now when attempting to transfer music between different devices.

If you’ve ever run into problems choosing the perfect color for your RGB smart lights in Google Home on iOS, check out the updated color wheel now rolling out.

In addition to all these improvements to the Home app and smart device operation, Google also shared its latest Gemini for Home enhancements today.

items.title: WhatsApp preps travel eSIM discovery, installation, and management tools
items.summary: WhatsApp could soon be your one-stop shop for all things eSIM.
items.body:
Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Mobile

WhatsApp preps travel eSIM discovery, installation, and management tools

WhatsApp could soon be your one-stop shop for all things eSIM.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 4:37 PM ET

•

•

Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• WhatsApp appears to be developing a system for eSIM discovery, purchase, installation, and management.

• Users would be able to search for eSIMs based on specific travel destinations.

• Automated tools could wait to activate the eSIM until you arrive where you’re headed.

WhatsApp just got a big upgrade with the announcement of support for scheduling messages, and now we’re already getting an early look at what could be coming next, as we uncover evidence for what looks like a new travel eSIM feature.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

You're reading an Android Authority exclusive story you won’t find anywhere else. An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

Looking across the changes present in WhatsApp’s version 2.26.47.10 update, we’re finding multiple references to “Travel eSIM” support. This isn’t yet live in the app, but here’s a preview for how one of the associated screens could be taking shape:

AssembleDebug / Android Authority

Internally, we’re seeing a whole lot of text strings that appear connected to this feature. Here are just a few:

Code

+Travel eSIM installed
+Keep WhatsApp open until it’s done.
+Installing travel eSIM…
+Getting your travel eSIM ready…
+Install it once and use with all your plans.
+Your travel eSIM is ready
+WhatsApp will add a travel eSIM to your phone. Your plan starts when your phone connects in %1$s.
+Install eSIM?
+This phone can’t take this eSIM. It may be locked to a carrier or out of eSIM space.
+Couldn’t install travel eSIM
+This eSIM’s activation code is invalid or has already been used.
+Couldn’t set up your travel eSIM
+Travel eSIMs aren’t available to you yet
+Your plan starts when you turn on your eSIM.
+Couldn’t load plans
+Loading data plans
+Plans aren’t available for this destination
+Your phone didn’t let WhatsApp install this eSIM.
+Installing an eSIM needs a phone with an eSIM chip and a recent version of Android.
+This phone can’t install eSIMs
+Install it now and turn it on when you arrive in %1$s.
+Your plan starts when your phone connects there. You’ll get a message when it does.

Based on what we’ve found so far, we can make a few guesses about how this is likely to operate. It seems that we’ll be able to enter a destination into the app, and WhatsApp would search for compatible eSIM options. Those may not be available for everyone, all at once, as we find “coming soon” messages prepared for both global and regional plans. Options may include fixed-data, as well as unlimited plans.

You can expect to see a few introductory screens helping to educate users about eSIMs, and it sure looks like the app is preparing to integrate with Android’s eSIM installation process.

One handy feature could be an automated system for turning on the eSIM only when we actually reach the destination we intended to use it — freeing us from accidentally plowing through our eSIM data before we really needed it.

Management tools should let you view the eSIMs you’ve purchased so far, seeing which are still available, which are expired, and which have data remaining on them. And along the way, it looks like the app will be able to give you low-data warnings or let you know when a plan is about to end.

Readers' poll

Would you use WhatsApp to buy and install eSIMs?

0 votes

Of course, there’s the possibility your phone may not support this functionality, especially if it’s running an older version of Android. For the moment, at least, we don’t yet have a clear sense for where that cutoff may lie, but expect there to be one.

Finally, WhatsApp might not be preparing this new support on its own, and a “Powered by %1$s” string could suggest that some of this eSIM system may arrive courtesy of a third-party service — we just don’t yet know whose name is going to show up in place of that variable.

All of this sounds pretty nice to our ears. Buying an eSIM is a great option for international travel, and WhatsApp is a great messaging service for travel abroad, so this feels like a match made in heaven. It also looks like WhatsApp is serious about its approach here, and the strings we’ve found paint the picture of quite robust integration. For now, we’ll keep looking for the rest of the details on how this new service offering could be coming together.

items.title: 1Password Security Breach: What Was Accessed and What Wasn't
items.summary: Popular password management app 1Password today said it experienced a security breach earlier this month. 1Password says some customer names and email addresses were accessed, but no customer vault contents were compromised. On November 19, 1Password saw indications that an employee's GitHub account…
items.body: Popular password management app 1Password today said it experienced a security breach earlier this month. 1Password says some customer names and email addresses were accessed, but no customer vault contents were compromised. On November 19, 1Password saw indications that an employee's GitHub account had been breached and began investigating. The company says the breached GitHub account was used to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, with the code downloading some customer data. Here's a list of what the hacker was able to get: Names and email addresses customers use to sign into 1Password Account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times Public keys Secure Remote Password protocol parameters (1Password says this can't be used for account access) Tokens in emailed links for invitations, provisioning, and account recovery Other non-secret account data related to 1Password's internal architecture, like version numeric identifiers and file numeric identifiers 1Password source code, which 1Password says does not include customer data or user secrets Access to 1Password's CI/CD system, which it says has infrastructure-related secrets for the service to work According to 1Password, there is no impact to its services, availability, or product security. Customer vaults and the items in them were not accessed, nor were the keys that protect vaults. The hacker did not have access to account recovery keys or 1Password apps and browser extensions. 1Password vaults are encrypted and protected by keys on the user end, so content is not accessible to 1Password or anyone who hacks the 1Password servers. The biggest risk comes from the token breach. Tokens can be used for account recovery, but they only work when paired with an SSO sign-in or a six-digit code sent to a user's email address. items.title: WhatsApp Finally Adds Scheduled Messages
items.summary: Popular messaging app WhatsApp was today updated with an option to schedule messages, which the company says was one of its most requested features. WhatsApp users can create a message and schedule it to arrive from 10 minutes to 14 days later in one-to-one chats and group chats. Scheduling a messag…
items.body: Popular messaging app WhatsApp was today updated with an option to schedule messages, which the company says was one of its most requested features. WhatsApp users can create a message and schedule it to arrive from 10 minutes to 14 days later in one-to-one chats and group chats. Scheduling a message can be done by pressing and holding the send button after composing and then choosing a date and time. Scheduled messages work with text, photos, and videos, and will still send even if a user's device is offline. There is an option to see all scheduled messages and delete them before they're sent if needed. Scheduled messages are end-to-end encrypted and look like any other WhatsApp message, with no indication on the receiver's end that the message was scheduled. Apple's iMessage service already has a Send Later feature that supports scheduling messages, so WhatsApp is catching up with Apple's built-in messaging option. WhatsApp says scheduled messages are rolling out globally over the coming weeks. items.title: Gemini for Home gets faster responses, smoother chats, and fixes for follow-up and music bugs
items.summary: Everyday voice commands should feel a little less frustrating.
items.body:
Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Smart home

Gemini for Home gets faster responses, smoother chats, and fixes for follow-up and music bugs

Everyday voice commands should feel a little less frustrating.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 3:15 PM ET

•

•

Joe Maring / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Google has fully rolled out speed improvements for common Gemini for Home smart home commands.

• The latest update fixes bugs affecting follow-up commands and stopping media playback.

• Google is also rolling out an improved Gemini Live experience, more expressive storytelling, and web answer sources on supported smart displays.

The story of Gemini for Home’s transition from Google Assistant is beginning to take a more positive turn. We’ve seen some users warming up to Google’s new voice assistant, particularly after noticeable improvements in response times. Now, Google is giving Gemini more polish, whether you’re asking it to switch off the lights or tell your kids a bedtime story.

With its second November update, Google has confirmed that speed improvements for common smart home commands have fully rolled out to Gemini for Home Early Access users. So, whether you’re turning on the lights or adjusting the thermostat, Gemini should respond and act faster.

Google has also fixed a bug where Gemini would occasionally forget the context of a conversation. For example, asking Gemini to turn the living room lights back on shortly after telling it to turn them off should now work as expected. Another fix addresses an issue where Gemini would incorrectly insist that nothing was playing when asked to stop music or other media.

Brady Snyder / Android Authority

Beyond these fixes, Google is beginning to roll out the upgraded Gemini Live experience it announced last week alongside energy-saving improvements for Nest thermostats and new features for Google Home cameras. Over the coming weeks, Google Home Premium subscribers will get faster, more natural conversations with Gemini, along with the ability to set timers, add reminders, and control smart home devices without ending an ongoing chat.

Gemini is also becoming a better storyteller. Starting today, stories will feature more expressive voices and varied pacing, and you can steer the plot as Gemini narrates. And if you own a supported smart display, you’ll be able to tap a new “Sources” option to see the websites Gemini used to answer your questions.

With Google Assistant set to retire from smart home devices in August 2027, every little improvement counts. And while more entertaining bedtime stories are a welcome addition, getting Gemini to remember which lights you were talking about is likely to make a bigger difference in everyday life.

items.title: Rumor: iOS 28 to Revamp Notifications
items.summary: Earlier today, we resurfaced a longstanding issue with Apple not consistently enforcing its rules related to iPhone apps advertising through notifications . It is a good time to share that we heard from multiple sources that Apple is planning to revamp the iPhone's notification system with iOS 28 ne…
items.body:
Rumor: iOS 28 to Revamp Notifications

Wednesday November 25, 2026 11:58 am PST by Joe Rossignol

Earlier today, we resurfaced a longstanding issue with Apple not consistently enforcing its rules related to iPhone apps advertising through notifications. It is a good time to share that we heard from multiple sources that Apple is planning to revamp the iPhone's notification system with iOS 28 next year.

The sources said iOS 28 will include significant changes to Notification Center, but we do not have any specific details. This is just a rumor. On Android 16 and later, you can filter notifications into News, Promotions, Social, and Suggested categories, and an equivalent iOS option if implemented would help to hide advertising clutter.

In the spot, a cyclops toy comes to life and becomes enamored with the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max. The toy takes photos, plays games, uses apps, listens to music, captures videos, makes calls, watches TV, and uses the flashlight for shadow puppets. The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max lasts through all of it, remaining at half charge when the cyclops's battery dies and the toy falls asleep. Apple's ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max lasts up to 30 hours in "typical use," which is based on median iPhone usage. The metric includes messages, photo taking, music, social app use, streaming, games, browsing, and navigation. The device lasts for up to 40 hours when streaming video, and up to 45 hours when watching downloaded videos. items.title: $799 Smart Glasses Promise Vision Pro-Style Controls in a 45g Frame
items.summary: Hong Kong startup Savage Technology has announced its first product, "Orrorin Glasses," promising Vision Pro-style pinch controls and full-color displays for both eyes in a frame weighing just 45 grams. The company describes the glasses as offering "Vision Pro–level interaction" and being around 25…
items.body: Hong Kong startup Savage Technology has announced its first product, "Orrorin Glasses," promising Vision Pro-style pinch controls and full-color displays for both eyes in a frame weighing just 45 grams. The company describes the glasses as offering "Vision Pro–level interaction" and being around 25 times lighter than Apple's headset, including its external battery. Savage highlights the bulky hardware currently required for Apple's spatial computing experience, although Orrorin offers substantially fewer capabilities. Savage says small pinches performed at the user's side control the interface without a ring, wristband, or controller. Eye tracking makes the display fade when the wearer looks away, rather than selecting interface elements as it does on Vision Pro. That also distinguishes Orrorin from the Meta Ray-Ban Display, which costs the same $799 but has a screen for only the right eye and requires a Neural Band wristband for gesture control. Standard Ray-Ban Meta glasses have no displays. Orrorin lacks positional tracking and spatial mapping , so it cannot anchor virtual windows in a room like Vision Pro. Orrorin is the first product from Savage Technology, co-founded by Bill Pei and Elena Shi, and remains in engineering validation for now. The company is currently targeting developers with third-party apps and interaction with AI agents such as Claude Code and Codex. Apple is expected to launch its first smart glasses next year , although the initial model reportedly will not have displays, instead offering speakers, microphones, and Siri integration. Orrorin reservations start at $29 toward the $799 price. Savage estimates shipments will begin in March 2027 for Founder Edition buyers and May 2027 for Early Bird buyers. items.title: Apple Has an iPhone Notifications Problem
items.summary: Apple has rules in place that are supposed to protect iPhone users from unwanted advertising in push notifications and Live Activities, but some apps appear to be flouting these rules, and Apple does not appear to be consistently enforcing them. Apple's App Store guidelines do allow iPhone apps to s…
items.body: Apple has rules in place that are supposed to protect iPhone users from unwanted advertising in push notifications and Live Activities, but some apps appear to be flouting these rules, and Apple does not appear to be consistently enforcing them. Apple's App Store guidelines do allow iPhone apps to send push notifications for promotions or direct marketing purposes, but only if users have "explicitly opted in to receive them via consent language displayed" in the app, and so long as the app provides a method "for a user to opt out from receiving such messages." The guideline, in part: Push Notifications should not be used for promotions or direct marketing purposes unless customers have explicitly opted in to receive them via consent language displayed in your app's UI, and you provide a method in your app for a user to opt out from receiving such messages. Unfortunately, there are some examples of apps ignoring this guideline. On my iPhone in Canada, there are several apps that send me push notifications containing promotions without offering a way to opt out of these promotion-specific notifications, such as Cineplex, McDonald's, and Wendy's. Canadian food delivery app Skip does offer a setting to turn off promotional notifications, but it has continued to send them to me long after I opted out. Do you have any iOS apps that don't respect your promo notification settings or don't let you turn off promo notifications as Apple requires? Let me know for a MacRumors story! items.title: 美国纽约州签署法案，限制汽车厂商对预装功能收取订阅费
items.summary: 2026年11月24日，美国纽约州州长凯西·霍楚尔签署一项编号为S.9348A/A.10411A的法案。该法案自2027年2月27日起生效，规定汽车制造商、经销商以及第三方服务提供商不得针对使用预装组件或硬件、且不会产生持续性成本的汽车功能，额外提供订阅服务或在车辆售出后收取费用。 法案将于2027年2月27日生效，违者每个销售点每次违规最高罚款250美元。 在法案签署前，汽车经销商莫霍克雪佛兰（MohawkChevrolet）总裁AndyGuelcher表示，订阅制有助于维持汽车基础售价，消费者可以按照自身需求启用部分功能。 https://www.news18a.com/~ https:/…
items.body:
美国纽约州签署法案，限制汽车厂商对预装功能收取订阅费

2026年11月24日，美国纽约州州长凯西·霍楚尔签署一项编号为S.9348A/A.10411A的法案。该法案自2027年2月27日起生效，规定汽车制造商、经销商以及第三方服务提供商不得针对使用预装组件或硬件、且不会产生持续性成本的汽车功能，额外提供订阅服务或在车辆售出后收取费用。
法案将于2027年2月27日生效，违者每个销售点每次违规最高罚款250美元。

在法案签署前，汽车经销商莫霍克雪佛兰（MohawkChevrolet）总裁AndyGuelcher表示，订阅制有助于维持汽车基础售价，消费者可以按照自身需求启用部分功能。

https://www.news18a.com/~
https://www.governor.ny.gov/~

说的就是方向盘/座椅加热、通风、CarPlay之类的不联网功能
